topic: 学术综合任务与转段检查
grammarFocus: 根据个人错题复查时态、从句、冠词、数量和主谓一致。
title: The Archive Audit: A Week 36 Reading Task
instructions: 阅读以下关于学术综合任务与转段检查的模拟材料（非官方雅思测试）。文章共约650词，包含A、B、C、D四个部分。请先通读全文，然后完成10道题目。题目类型包括单选、填空、匹配（以单选形式）和判断正误/未提及。填空答案必须来自原文，且不超过规定字数。所有解释均为中文，并附原文证据。注意：本材料为模拟练习，不是官方雅思测试，也不代表真实雅思分数。
passage:
A. When Mira Chen, a second-year doctoral candidate in environmental history, received an email from the university archive asking her to audit a collection of 19th-century farming diaries, she expected a straightforward task. The archive had recently digitised 200 diaries and wanted a researcher to check the metadata—the descriptive labels attached to each file. Mira assumed she would spend two weeks comparing the digital records with the original handwritten books. However, the project quickly became more complex than she had anticipated. The archive's head librarian, Dr. Evans, had mentioned that the collection was fragile, but Mira had not realised how much this would affect her work.

B. The first problem appeared on day three. Mira noticed that several diaries had been labelled with the wrong decade. For example, a diary written in 1887 had been tagged as 1878. When she reported this to the archive's digital manager, he explained that the error had occurred during an automated scanning process. The software had misread handwritten dates, especially when the ink was faded. Mira realised that she needed to check every date manually, which would take far longer than two weeks. She also discovered that some diaries contained loose pages inserted by the original writers. These pages had been scanned separately but not linked to the main diary files. As a result, the digital collection was incomplete. She estimated that at least thirty diaries were affected by this problem, and she began to keep a separate list of every missing page she found. This list would later become an important part of her final report. In addition, she noticed that the handwriting in some diaries was extremely difficult to read, which slowed her progress further.

C. By the end of the first month, Mira had developed a systematic approach. She created a spreadsheet that listed each diary's correct date, author, and location. She also noted any missing pages and cross-referenced them with the physical books. Her supervisor, Professor Alan Reid, suggested that she present her findings at the department's monthly research seminar. Mira was nervous because she had never presented to a large group before. Nevertheless, she agreed. During her presentation, she explained that the archive's metadata contained three main types of errors: incorrect dates, missing links between pages, and inconsistent author names. She recommended that the archive adopt a manual checking procedure for all future digitisation projects. The audience asked several questions, and Mira answered them confidently. After the seminar, Professor Reid told her that her work had been excellent and that she should consider writing a short article for the archive's newsletter. He also mentioned that the archive had received a small grant to improve its digital records.

D. Reflecting on the project, Mira realised that the initial task description had been misleading. The archive had described the job as a simple metadata check, but it had actually required historical research skills, technical problem-solving, and clear communication. She also learned that she needed to ask more questions at the beginning of a project. If she had clarified the archive's expectations earlier, she could have saved time. Now, as she begins to write her article, she feels more prepared for future collaborative projects. The archive has invited her to return next year to help train new volunteers. Mira has already started planning a short training session for them, focusing on how to spot common metadata errors. She believes that sharing her experience will help the archive avoid similar problems in the future. She also plans to include a checklist of common errors in her article, which she hopes will be useful for other researchers.

grammar.title: 时态、从句、冠词、数量和主谓一致复习
grammar.explanation: 本部分针对你在错题复查中常见的语法点进行复习。请先理解句意，再注意形式。1. 时态：过去完成时表示过去某一时间前已完成的动作（如had developed）。2. 从句：定语从句用who/which/that引导；宾语从句用that引导。3. 冠词：定冠词the表示特指，不定冠词a/an表示泛指。4. 数量：可数名词复数与many/few连用，不可数名词与much/little连用。5. 主谓一致：主语为单数时谓语用单数，主语为复数时谓语用复数；注意集合名词和不定代词。
grammar.example: By the end of the first month, Mira had developed a systematic approach. (过去完成时)

options: She had finished the report before the meeting started.
She has finished the report before the meeting started.
She finished the report before the meeting has started.
She had finish the report before the meeting started.
answers: She had finished the report before the meeting started.
questions.explanation: 过去完成时（had + 过去分词）表示在过去某一时间点之前已经完成的动作。这里‘完成报告’发生在‘会议开始’之前，所以用had finished。
questions.evidence: 语法规则：过去完成时用于表示过去某一时间前已完成的动作。

options: The book which I borrowed from the library is very interesting.
The book who I borrowed from the library is very interesting.
The book which I borrowed from the library are very interesting.
The book which I borrowed from the library is very interested.
answers: The book which I borrowed from the library is very interesting.
questions.explanation: 定语从句修饰物用which/that，不用who；主语the book是单数，谓语用is；interesting修饰物，interested修饰人。
questions.evidence: 语法规则：定语从句中，指物用which/that，指人用who。

options: She is an honest researcher and a university professor.
She is a honest researcher and an university professor.
She is an honest researcher and an university professor.
She is a honest researcher and a university professor.
answers: She is an honest researcher and a university professor.
questions.explanation: honest以元音音素开头，用an；university以辅音音素/juː/开头，用a。
questions.evidence: 语法规则：不定冠词a用于辅音音素前，an用于元音音素前。

questions.evidence: 语法规则：many修饰可数名词复数，much/little修饰不可数名词。
